sentences.text: 4. Learned advocate Mr. H. R. Kapadia submits that he has received instructions to appear on behalf of the original complainant.
He strongly opposes the present application inter-alia contending that the applicant is a habitual offender and there are 21 antecedents against the present applicant.
Therefore, he submits that the present application may not be allowed.

5. The learned APP appearing for the respondent State vehemently opposes the present application submitting that as per modus operandi of the present applicant, forged power attorney in the name of one Ayeshaben was prepared by the applicant and thumb impression of the first informant and his brother were also made on the said document, by which land in question came to be transferred to one Ayeshaben. It appears from the papers of investigation that there is no person named,
Ayeshaben and the applicant has sold the land to Ayeshaben on the basis of forged documents.

Therefore, she submits that the offences which have been charged, are serious in nature and looking to the facts as well as the allegations made against the applicant, no discretion would be required to be exercised.
6. I have heard learned advocates appearing for the parties and perused the papers of investigation.
From the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11589/2023 ORDER DATED: 19/10/2023 undefined record it appears that the investigation is over and Charge-sheet has already been filed.

It appears from the papers that the role attributed to the present applicant is to the effect that the applicant has executed power of attorney in the name of one Ayeshaben with forged signature and thumb impression of the first informant and his brother and on the basis of said power of attorney,
sale-deed came to be executed in favour of Ayeshaben.
In the said sale-deed also, forged signature and thumb impression of the first informant and his brother were affixed by the present applicant.
The FSL report indicates that the signature and thumb impression affixed on the documents had matched with the thumb impression and signature of the present applicant.
The record also indicates that both documents i.e. sale-deed and power of attorney have been recovered from the custody of the present applicant.
It also reveals from the record that no person named Ayeshaben ever existed.
Thus, on the basis of documents in question, present applicant had usurped the land belonging to the first informant and his brother.
Considering the said facts investigation is over and Charge-sheet is filed, so also the fact that the trial is not likely to be concluded in a year, the present application deserves to be allowed.

7. In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of allegations made in the FIR and without discussing the evidence in details as well as NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11589/2023 ORDER DATED: 19/10/2023 undefined without going into details,
prima-facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion to enlarge the applicant on bail.

Hence, the application is allowed and the applicant is ordered to be released on bail in connection with F.I.R. No.11191045230150 of 2023 registered with Sola High Court Police Station, District Ahmedabad, on executing a bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand only) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court and subject to the conditions that;
(a) not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the fact of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any Police Officer or tamper with the evidence.

It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions in accordance with law.
9. At the trial, the concerned trial Court shall not be influenced by the prima facie observations made by this Court in the present order.
10. Rule made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
